messages.content: Write an internal proposal asking leadership for a quarter of engineering time to pay down technical debt. Around 250 words.

Here's a draft. The bracketed figures are placeholders — put your own numbers in, since the argument only works if the counts are real.

---

**Proposal: one quarter of engineering time for debt paydown**

**Ask:** Give Q[X] to debt work in [the billing service and the shared auth layer]. The [N]-person platform team ships no new roadmap features for those twelve weeks.

**Why now.** Median time from PR open to merge is [4.5] days, against [1.8] a year ago. CI runs [38] minutes and fails for no reason about [one run in six], so engineers have stopped believing it and merge after a re-run. Three of our last five Sev-2 incidents came back to the same untested config path in billing. This quarter's debt gets paid either way. Right now we pay it in unplanned incident weekends and in features that slip twice before they land.

**What we'd do.** Break the config path apart and put a test harness around it. Retire the [2016-era] job runner that only [two engineers] can touch safely. Get CI under [15] minutes by parallelizing the integration suite.

**What we'd measure.** Median merge time, CI wall-clock, spurious failure rate, Sev-2 count. Weekly reporting, with a baseline taken before we start. If merge time hasn't moved by week eight, we stop and reassess instead of finishing the plan out of stubbornness.

**The cost.** [Two] roadmap items slip a quarter: [feature A] and [feature B]. Both are worth less than the interest we're paying.

I'd rather ask for this now than after the next incident.

---

~250 words. Send me the real numbers and the actual systems and I'll tighten it into something you can forward.
Rewrite the text above. Keep the same length and the same purpose. Return only the rewritten text.
